column1: # That check reads every backticked token in a `status: binding` instruction
# doc, in CLAUDE.md, and every bare token in instance/params.yaml, and fails
# when a token that looks like a repo-relative path does not exist. Absence is
# a FAIL, never a skip: a rule with no predicate is the defect this file's
# Format: source<TAB>path<TAB>reason<TAB>note. Keyed on the source+path PAIR,
# never on the source alone -- a whole-file exemption would silently license
# every future dangling path added to that file under the original, unrelated
# justification (the lesson already paid for in instance/unit-path-exemptions.tsv).
# reason is a closed vocabulary; an unknown value is a hard FAIL:
#   illustrative   a placeholder path in an example, never meant to resolve
#   external       outside this repository's tree (another repo, a host path)
#   planned        deliberately not built yet, tracked in its own row
#   generated      a deliberately untracked runtime artifact -- presence is host
#                  state, so the stale-exemption check does not apply to it
#   pending-<row>  a citation believed FALSE, awaiting the row named here
# An exemption is a DEBT, not a dismissal. Every row reports as a WARN so it
# stays visible; a row nobody consults is a FAIL; and a row whose path now
# exists is a FAIL, so an exemption cannot outlive the reason it was granted.
# The pending-V3-2.13 rows below are the findings of
# instance/audits/false-facts-2026-08-04.md plus six the widened check found on
# its own. V3-2.13 landed the mechanism deliberately without fixing them: some
# are genuine deletions, some want a redirect, and gate/land-batch.sh is a
# policy question (should the batch path exist at all) rather than a broken
# reference. Each becomes its own row now that the checker names it.
